before.title: 1.0 Kappa Engine Oil Seepage and Plastic Coolant Hose Leaks
before.description: The Ray's 1.0L Kappa engine uses an aluminum block and head with a thin head/valve-cover gasket that is sensitive to heat cycling. Korean owner communities and used-car inspection guides consistently flag oil seepage around the gaskets and valve cover as the Ray's most common chronic problem on aging first-generation cars. A related weak point is the plastic coolant/heater hose connectors, which deform and crack with heat over time, causing slow coolant loss — turbo (TCI) variants are reported to be especially prone because of higher underhood temperatures. Left unaddressed, low coolant on the small-displacement engine can lead to overheating.
before.solution: Replace the leaking valve cover/head gasket (roughly 100,000–200,000 KRW in Korea) and replace degraded plastic coolant/heater hoses and connectors (roughly 100,000–150,000 KRW). On any used Ray, check the engine bay for oil residue, monitor coolant level regularly, and inspect for wet spots under the car; address seepage early before it progresses.
symptoms: Oil residue around valve cover and gasket edges
Oil smell or light smoke from the engine bay after driving
Coolant level slowly dropping between services
Coolant stains or drips under the front of the car
Sweet coolant smell with the heater on

before.title: 2023+ Ray EV Integrated Charging Control Unit Overcurrent — Slow Charging Fails (Service Campaign)
before.description: Shortly after the Ray EV's late-2023 relaunch (35.2 kWh LFP battery, 7 kW AC charging), Kia opened a free-repair campaign covering 3,787 vehicles built between September 20, 2023 and January 4, 2024 — effectively every unit sold to that point. When connected to certain slow (AC) chargers, an overcurrent condition can occur inside the integrated charging control unit, illuminating warning lights and preventing the car from charging. Kia is fixing the defect with an improved software update, with the campaign running through August 13, 2026. Separately, early 2023 Ray EVs were reported unable to charge on some older public slow chargers, prompting Korea's Ministry of Environment to publish a list of incompatible charger models.
before.solution: Have the free service campaign performed at a Kia service center: an improved software update for the integrated charging control unit (campaign deadline August 13, 2026). Until updated, if charging stops with a warning light on a particular charger, retry on a different/newer slow charger, and consult the Ministry of Environment's incompatible-charger notice for chargers to avoid.
symptoms: Warning light comes on during slow (AC) charging
Charging session aborts or never starts on certain public chargers
Car charges normally on some chargers but not others
Charging error message on the instrument cluster

before.title: Drive Belt 'Cricket' Chirp From Solid Alternator Pulley (2011–2013 Builds)
before.description: Rays built through roughly 2013 came with a solid (fixed) alternator pulley instead of an overrunning alternator pulley (OAP)/auto-tensioner arrangement. As the serpentine belt stretches with age, it slips on the solid pulley and produces a distinctive high-pitched chirping that Korean owners universally describe as a 'cricket noise' (귀뚜라미 소리), most noticeable during acceleration or when the A/C compressor loads the belt. It is one of the best-known quirks of early Rays in the Korean owner community. The noise itself is benign, but a badly slipping belt accelerates belt and bearing wear and can eventually affect charging.
before.solution: Replace the solid alternator pulley with the updated OAP-type pulley along with a new serpentine belt (roughly 200,000–500,000 KRW in Korea depending on whether alternator bearings are also replaced). On 2013+ cars with the updated pulley the noise is far less common; a belt dressing or tension adjustment is only a temporary fix.
symptoms: High-pitched chirping or squealing like a cricket from the engine bay
Noise worsens during acceleration
Noise appears or gets louder when the A/C is switched on
Noise changes with engine RPM, not road speed

before.title: Early Ray Engine Stall With A/C On — ECU/Climate Control Logic Error (2012 Service Campaign)
before.description: Kia ran a public free-repair campaign (무상수리) in July 2012 covering 11,439 Rays built between November 28, 2011 and May 25, 2012 that were equipped with full automatic temperature control (FATC). A logic error between the ECU and the automatic climate control system could destabilize engine RPM — or stall the engine outright — when the driver braked while coasting with the air conditioning running and no throttle applied. The condition typically appeared at low speed in stop-and-go driving, exactly when an unexpected stall is most disruptive.
before.solution: Kia reprogrammed both the ECU and the automatic temperature control unit free of charge at its service centers starting July 9, 2012. Any remaining unrepaired early-build Ray should receive the updated ECU/FATC calibration; used-car buyers should confirm the campaign was performed.
symptoms: Engine RPM fluctuates when braking with the A/C on
Engine stalls while coasting to a stop in traffic
Idle becomes unstable at low speed with the compressor engaged
Problem only occurs when air conditioning is running

before.title: ECU Software Defect Causing Engine Stall While Driving (2026 Recall)
before.description: In April 2026, Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) announced a recall of 220,059 Kia Ray vehicles built between December 5, 2019 and August 8, 2025 — the largest single recall in that announcement batch. The engine control unit (ECU) software was found to be inadequately designed, creating a risk that the 1.0L Kappa engine shuts off unexpectedly while the car is being driven. A stall in traffic disables power-assisted systems and creates a collision risk, which is why MOLIT classified it as a safety defect. Corrective action (free ECU reprogramming at Kia service centers) began March 28, 2026.
before.solution: Have the recall performed free of charge at any Kia service center or Auto-Q shop: the ECU software is updated (reprogrammed) to the corrected calibration. Owners can check whether their VIN is included at the Korean automobile recall center (car.go.kr). Owners who paid out of pocket for related repairs before the recall can claim reimbursement from Kia.
symptoms: Engine suddenly shuts off while driving
Loss of throttle response before the stall
Power steering and brake assist feel heavy after stall
Warning lights illuminate when the engine cuts out
Engine restarts normally after the stall

before.title: First-Generation Ray EV On-Board Charger (OBC) Failure
before.description: The original Ray EV (2012–2017, Korea's first mass-produced passenger EV, ~2,000–3,000 units mostly sold to fleets and early adopters) has a well-documented on-board charger weakness. The OBC that converts AC to DC for slow charging lacks adequate thermal protection for its circuitry; heat generated during charging can cause sparks or errors that burn the capacitors. Korean owner communities report the failure as near-universal by around 60,000 km of charge cycling, and Kia never issued a formal campaign. An official Kia service center quotes roughly 2.5 million KRW for a complete OBC replacement on an old, low-value EV, though independent specialists repair the board for around 400,000 KRW. Owners also face the added burden that the car's CHAdeMO DC fast-charge standard is increasingly unsupported at Korean public chargers, making a working OBC (slow charge) essential to keep the car usable.
before.solution: If slow charging fails with a burnt-capacitor OBC, either replace the OBC assembly at a Kia service center (~2.5M KRW / ~$1,900) or have the OBC board repaired at an independent EV electronics specialist (~400,000 KRW / ~$300). Used buyers should test AC slow charging to full before purchase and budget for an OBC repair on any high-mileage example.
symptoms: Slow (AC) charging stops working entirely
Charging error or warning light when plugged into a slow charger
Burning smell or popping noise from charger area during AC charging
DC fast charging still works while AC charging does not
Charge percentage stops rising mid-session
